name: Akihabara
description: Akihabara's Electric Town from open data, lit by the real sun: Chuo-dori's signs, the station's Electric Town exit, Kanda Myojin up the hill, and Nikolai-do over Ochanomizu.

imagery.attribution: Geospatial Information Authority of Japan (GSI) seamless aerial photographs (GSI terms of use, source attribution)

terrain.attribution: GSI Fundamental Geospatial Data DEM5A, 5 m airborne laser survey bare earth (GSI terms of use); 10 m DEM where 5A is absent

terrain_check.name: GSI elevation API (1 m laser DEM where flown, otherwise DEM5)

plateau.attribution: MLIT Project PLATEAU Tokyo 23 wards LOD2 building models (CC BY 4.0), as vector tiles by indigo-lab (MIT)

seawall.note: The rivers' and the bay's revetments and the castle moats: granite blocks and concrete.

trees.note: Species are not mapped. Elms stand for the zelkovas of Kanda Myojin's grove, plane trees for Chuo-dori's and Kuramaebashi-dori's street trees. A guess, not a survey.

minor_labels: マーチ エキュート 神田万世橋

tour.title: Akihabara, from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings. {share:plateau}% of the footprint area stands at a height Project PLATEAU surveyed, on GSI's 5 m laser-scanned bare earth.

tour.title: Electric Town after dark
tour.text: Chuo-dori from Manseibashi to Suehirocho: radio parts after the war, then computers, games and anime. The signs and prints here are typical of the street, not its real shops'.

tour.title: Up the hill
tour.text: West of the tracks the ground rises to the Kanda heights: Kanda Myojin's gate, and Nikolai-do's green dome over Ochanomizu.

sources.landmarks: Kanda Myojin's Zuishinmon (1975) on OpenStreetMap's footprint, its proportions from photographs; Nikolai-do's dome (about 35 m to the cross; Japanese Orthodox Church) on its drum. Electric Town's signs and prints are indicative: typical trades and invented adverts, no real shops' signs or logos.
sources.fonts: Signs drawn with Google Fonts under the SIL Open Font License: Zen Kaku Gothic New, Dela Gothic One, M PLUS Rounded 1c, DotGothic16, Bebas Neue, Reggae One, Shippori Mincho

night.note: Electric Town's signs are lit landmark meshes (city.py); the streets' lamps are the country's defaults.

weather.source: Tokyo (Kitanomaru Park): Japan Meteorological Agency, 1991-2020 normals, days with at least 0.5 mm

game.title: Akihabara on Foot
game.blurb: Walk Akihabara under the real sun: Chuo-dori's signs and wall prints, the lanes of parts shops and arcades, and up the hill to Kanda Myojin and Nikolai-do.

areas.name: 秋葉原
areas.note: Electric Town: where a game sends you to buy parts and play retro games

Radio Kaikan, the corner ラジオ会館前
Kanda Myojin, the gate 隨神門
Nikolai-do, the gate ニコライ堂前

npcs.name: Yuto 悠斗
npcs.role: Parts shop owner パーツ屋
idle: After the war this was a black market for radio parts, under the tracks. Then TVs, then PCs, then games.
Junk boxes still: a hundred yen a cable. {time}.

npcs.name: Mai 舞
idle: お帰りなさいませ! Welcome home. Flyers, flyers. The cafe's on the fifth floor.
We say 'welcome home', not 'welcome'. It's a game everyone plays.

npcs.name: Taku 拓
idle: Junk Street. The shops here sell cartridges by the kilo, if you know where to look.
The arcade by the station has a cabinet from 1987 that still eats coins. {sun_line}

npcs.name: Emi 恵美
idle: Kanda Myojin is Akihabara's shrine. We sell charms to protect your computer. Really.
The festival is in May, in odd years. The portable shrines go right down Chuo-dori.

quests.title: Electric Town
talk: Welcome to Akiba! I'm Yuto. My father sold radio parts under these tracks; I sell everything else.
Chuo-dori is the main street; the lanes behind it are where things happen. Mai hands out flyers on the corner.

quests.title: Welcome home
talk: Every weekend afternoon Chuo-dori closes to cars: 歩行者天国, the pedestrians' heaven. Come back on a Sunday.
Taku knows the lanes. He's on Junk Street, north of the arcades.

quests.title: Junk Street
talk: Look up at the blade signs: パーツ, 中古, 買取, レトロゲーム. Every floor a different shop.
Pick a door and climb. In Akiba the best shop is always on the top floor, and the lift is always broken.

quests.title: Kanda Myojin
talk: Up the hill from Electric Town: Kanda Myojin, the shrine of Edo's merchants, now of its programmers.
And further, over the river, Nikolai-do's green dome. Go and listen for its bells.
